notes.meaning: Job begins his reply to Zophar with biting sarcasm. He mocks his friends for acting as if they alone possess all human wisdom and as if wisdom will die with them. Their proud attitude has offered him neither comfort nor real answers.

Job insists that he has a mind of his own and is not inferior to his friends. The grand theological truths they have shared are common knowledge that anyone can grasp. Job knows these basic facts about God just as well as they do.

Job laments that his own friends are laughing at him in his misery. In the past, he prayed to God and received answers, yet now this righteous man has become a laughingstock. His pain proves that being faithful to God does not shield a person from terrible suffering in this life.

People who live in ease and comfort often look down on those who suffer. When someone slips into hardship, the prosperous treat him like an old, burned-out torch that is tossed away. They wrongly assume that calamity only strikes people who deserve to fall.

Job points out that real life contradicts his friends' simple rules. Violent robbers often dwell safely in their tents, and people who openly provoke God seem peaceful and wealthy. Earthly success is no proof of God's favor, nor is suffering proof of His anger.

Job tells his friends to look at nature for basic instruction. The animals, birds, earth, and fish all clearly display how God made and rules the world. Even simple creatures show that life and suffering are under God's control without needing human philosophy to explain it.

Job declares that all of creation knows the Lord's hand has done this. The life of every animal and the breath of every human being belong entirely to Him. God alone holds the absolute right to give life or take it away as He sees fit.

Just as the tongue tastes food to see what is good, the mind's ear must test the words it hears. Job reminds his friends that people must weigh what they are taught rather than accepting old sayings without thinking. He has tested their speeches and found them empty.

People often expect the elderly to possess wisdom because they have lived many years. Job grants that long experience can teach many things, but human elders are still limited and can make mistakes. He prepares to show that perfect, unfailing wisdom belongs only to God.

True wisdom and absolute power belong to God alone. He possesses all counsel and understanding, needing no advice from any human being. All creaturely knowledge is only a small gift borrowed from His boundless source.

When God tears something down, no human power can rebuild it. If He shuts a person up in prison or trouble, nobody can release that person without His permission. He has total control over what stands and what falls in human life.

God commands the waters of the earth as absolute ruler. If He holds back the rain, rivers dry up and the ground parches, but if He unleashes the waters, they can flood and overturn the land. The natural world obeys His will completely.

God possesses lasting power and sound wisdom. Both the person who is tricked and the person who tricks others are under His sovereign control, meaning His supreme rule over all things. He directs even human folly and schemes to accomplish His own righteous purposes.

God can easily humble the most trusted political advisers. He strips wise counselors of their dignity and shows that esteemed judges are actually fools. Human wisdom fails the moment God decides to frustrate worldly plans.

God breaks the authority of earthly kings and reduces them to the status of bound captives or servants. He leads priests away stripped of their sacred robes and overthrows long-established rulers. Neither high royal rank nor religious office can shield leaders when God brings them low.

God silences the most gifted speakers and removes good judgment from seasoned community leaders. He pours disgrace upon noble rulers and disarms the strength of mighty warriors. Every human gift of leadership vanishes as soon as God withdraws it.

God uncovers the deepest secrets that were hidden in thick darkness. He brings secret plots and things buried in the shadow of death into plain daylight. Nothing in heaven or on earth is too hidden for Him to expose.

God directs the rise and fall of whole nations throughout history. He allows a people to grow great and expand, and then He can destroy or scatter them at His will. The destiny of empires does not depend on human might, but on God's sovereign plan.

God strips the world's rulers of their reason and leaves them lost in a pathless desert. Deprived of understanding, they grope about in the dark and stagger like drunken men. Rulers who thought they were masters of the earth become utterly helpless when God takes away their wisdom.
